title: SSL/TLS Certificates Renewal Counted Before a Domain Retry
content:
> Harborline Customer Accounts, for the customer's certificate subscription on SSL/TLS Certificates

## Which certificate and what it is charged

The certificate subscription the top-up counts is the customer's active certificate subscription with auto-renew on when its next auto-renew attempt falls before the retry; a certificate has no retry days, so its single attempt day is the SSL charter's auto-renew day before the subscription end date. Because every auto-renew charge in any category tries credit first, the top-up covers this charge in full when its next auto-renew attempt falls from today up to the day before the retry, which credit would otherwise pay first. Its charge is the auto-renew charge the SSL/TLS Certificates published auto-renew rule sets, whichever source pays it. The top-up's certificate renews for the years of its latest term line, its latest renewal or auto-renew line or, where none has been billed, its purchase line, at most the product's maximum subscription years.

## The certificate price component

| Renewal years | Certificate price component |
|---|---|
| 3 | the product's 3-year price per year times 3 |
| 2 | the product's 2-year price per year times 2 |
| 1 | the product's 1-year price |
| otherwise | no certificate charge is counted |

## From the price component to the charge

1. The certificate price component is reduced by the account tier's SSL discount.
2. The extra names are billed without that percentage, at the product's price per year for each extra name, for each name and each year renewed. On a renewal of two or three years each name's yearly price is multiplied by the product's per-year price for that term divided by its 1-year price, and on such a renewal the names after the first 10 are taken at 0.6 of that price up to the first 50 names and at 0.4 of it beyond them. On a one-year renewal every extra name is billed at the full yearly price.
3. The reduced amount, the reduced certificate price component together with the extra-name amount, is rounded half up to the cent.
4. An OV or EV product whose organisation validation, counted as the days from the date it last completed to the current subscription end date plus 365, would be older than the product's organisation validation reuse days then adds a re-vetting fee of $29.00 for an OV product or $49.00 for an EV product.
5. A covered domain that is an active Harborline registration then takes off a Harborline domain credit of $6.00 on Harborline DNS or $3.00 on external nameservers.
6. The result is rounded half up to the cent.

The charge so found enters the credit the retry needs.

## Worked example (hypothetical product figures)

An OV subscription renewing for three years, with a 1-year price of $70.00, a 3-year price per year of $56.00, an extra-name price of $8.00 per year and 3 extra names, on an account with a 20 percent SSL discount; its organisation validation stays within the reuse limit, and its covered domain is an active Harborline registration on external nameservers.

- Price component: $56.00 times 3, $168.00, reduced by 20 percent to $134.40.
- Name yearly price: $8.00 times $56.00 divided by $70.00, $6.40; 3 names, all within the first 10. Extra names: $6.40 times 3 times 3 years, $57.60.
- Reduced amount: $134.40 plus $57.60, $192.00. No re-vetting fee. Harborline domain credit $3.00: $189.00.
